gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/initial recommended=1

This PR, which you wrote, adds a CSV export download to widgets; robin and the acme/reviewers team are also requested reviewers. It covers the CSV download and its header format, defers scheduled exports to acme/widgets#46, builds the whole CSV in memory before sending it instead of streaming it (a difference the spec records on purpose), and leaves the export screen to acme/export-ui.

Two problems block merging.

1. The CSV export leaves out the header row, so a spreadsheet that opens the file has no column names. The local test export_header in tests/export.test.mjs fails on this (src/export.ts:31).
2. The export guide says exports run nightly, but the button exports only when someone clicks it, so a reader would wait for a file that never arrives on its own (docs/export.md:8). A fix that makes the guide describe the on-demand button is drafted.

maria pointed out the missing header in a PR comment, and the drafted reply agrees and says the fix is coming. A required check, unit, is still running. The build check passed in CI, and the local test run failed only on the header test. Your earlier review raised 3 items, and 2 of them are now addressed. The rebase onto main succeeded after one conflict in src/export.ts was resolved, and the rebased branch was pushed. One smaller point does not block merging: the export loop repeats the paging code that a shared helper already provides (src/export.ts:44), and deliver with nits can take it.

I recommend deliver because both problems have repairs ready and this is your own PR.

Pick one:
1. deliver - repair blockers, rebase on main, watch CI, repeat until merge is offered. [recommended]
2. deliver with nits - the same, and also replace the repeated paging code with the shared helper.
3. assess - post the two problems to the PR as one review and make no repairs.
4. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

The Change concerns contract-change judging, which this case does not exercise. Three After drifts sit close to the line and are worth tightening. First, A's sync sentence drops the supplied "no commits were dropped" and adds "the rebased branch was pushed", which the snapshot never states; keep the sync prose to the supplied outcome (rebased onto main, one conflict in src/export.ts resolved, no commits dropped). Second, C's deliver row now says "delivery course" and "sync attempts", which is unexplained internal vocabulary that Before avoided with "repair attempts" and "branch updates"; restore the plain terms. Third, the stop rows changed between snapshots (A removes the worktree unconditionally, B mentions "the checkout", C says "if it is clean") and no longer say the run ends; pin one stop wording so cleanup conditions are not implied or dropped. In the evidence record, "AC outcomes" and "Check dispositions: none" add terms the rest of the report never explains; they are tolerable only because they sit behind show evidence, so keep them out of the report prose.
